A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaRFT research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix A report original model-training experiments, mathematical benchmark results, efficiency measurements and curriculum ablations.

after.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix A report original benchmark evaluations, training-efficiency results and analyses of curriculum settings and difficulty estimation.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains nearest-difficulty batch selection, binary correctness rewards and the clipped tanh difficulty update. Section 3.1 adds a rationale for deterministic selection; Gaussian sampling is mentioned only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the DeepScaleR training distributions, including the extreme-difficulty scenarios, and the same six evaluation benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH 500, OlympiadBench, Minerva Math, AMC 23 and AIME 24. The extreme scenarios move from Appendix A.3 to Section 5.4.

E2.justification: PPO, filtered-data PPO and fixed-curriculum PPO remain the comparators in Figure 3 and Tables 1–2. The relocated GRPO, REINFORCE++ and difficulty-estimation comparisons also retain their original participants.

E3.justification: Model configurations, training sample counts, pass@128 difficulty scoring, evaluation intervals, AMC/AIME response averaging and Table 3 hyperparameters are unchanged. The new explanation of excluded scoring costs clarifies existing timing measurements without establishing a changed evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The target-reward ablation, extreme-difficulty tests, fixed-curriculum dynamics, alternative-RL comparisons and LLM-based difficulty analysis are retained. Moving v3 Appendices A.2–A.5 into v4 Sections 5.3–5.6 adds no new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Sections 5.2 and 5.5 newly disclose single-seed results, including one seed per configuration for final accuracy. No additional runs or confidence intervals are reported; the existing fixed ±1% shading and difficulty-estimation sampling trials remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain all numerical entries, and the eight scientific figures retain their plotted results. For example, both versions report 40.48% for AdaRFT and 37.41% for PPO on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B under skew-difficult training. Figure relocation and claim qualifications do not change these outcomes.

T1.justification: Equation 1 corrects the policy normalization factor from Z(x) to 1/Z(x). Section 3.4 removes the inference that the KL lower bound establishes proportional gradient magnitude and explicitly limits its implications for optimal learning. The Appendix B.2 controller derivation is retained.

C1.justification: The central adaptive-curriculum contribution remains, but the abstract, introduction and conclusion qualify the speedup as applying to RFT with existing difficulty annotations. Claims of significant final-accuracy improvement are narrowed to maintaining or often improving accuracy in the reported runs.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly explains the excluded upfront scoring cost, its importance for one-off runs and possible amortization. Sections 3.4 and 5.2 qualify the theoretical motivation and single-seed accuracy evidence. Section 3.1 also adds a deterministic-sampling rationale and discusses a possible diversity tradeoff.

D1.justification: Section 6 explicitly documents 1.28 million scorer rollouts for pass@128 scoring of 10,000 examples and states that Table 1 excludes this work. The implementation settings, four-page difficulty prompt, and code and dataset access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and basic novelty positioning are retained. Expanded author lists and bibliographic URLs are presentation changes; Team et al. becoming Kimi et al. refers to the same Kimi k1.5 work.

P1.justification: Four appendix analyses become main-text Sections 5.3–5.6, and the former Limitations section is condensed into Discussion before the conclusion. Claims and theoretical explanations are edited, author affiliations change, and the ARR-specific LLM-writing disclosure in Appendix C is removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a single-column TMLR layout, with a redesigned author block, publication headers and reflowed tables and references. Figures are substantially relocated: v3 Figures 5–8 become main-text Figures 4–7, while v3 Figure 4 becomes appendix Figure 8.

improvement.justification: V4 corrects Equation 1 and improves the calibration of its claims by acknowledging single-seed accuracy evidence and excluding upfront difficulty scoring from the reported speedup. These changes make the existing evidence more accurately interpretable. The method and empirical support remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
